name: Digital Crossroad

profile.reading:
Digital Crossroad's Indiana facility, known as DX-1, sits in Hammond, Indiana, on the state line with Illinois and less than thirty minutes from downtown Chicago. The site is an adaptive reuse of the former State Line Generating Plant, a coal fired power station that operated on the Lake Michigan shoreline through much of the twentieth century before its retirement, and the surrounding campus includes a 10,000 square foot technology incubator housed in the former State Line Archway building, a structure the operator notes historically served as office space connected to Thomas Edison. Converting a retired power plant site into a data center campus is a pattern seen at a handful of former utility properties around the country, since the sites already carry heavy duty electrical infrastructure and interconnections that a new data center can reuse rather than build from scratch.

DX-1 itself is a 105,000 square foot building with more than 72,000 square feet of data hall space available to customers. Digital Crossroad states the facility is built to Tier III concurrently maintainable standards, supports up to 20 megawatts of critical IT load, and can draw on a substation with more than 100 megawatts of on site capacity for future phases, with individual racks supporting up to 25 kilowatts of density. The operator reports a design power usage effectiveness of 1.15, a relatively efficient figure that it attributes in part to using Lake Michigan water side economization for cooling alongside outside air cooling and Munters refrigerant based units, reducing reliance on mechanical chilling for much of the year. The facility holds ISO 27001 and SOC 2 certifications, common benchmarks for information security and operational controls in colocation.

On connectivity, Digital Crossroad advertises being fewer than twelve fiber route miles from 350 East Cermak Road in Chicago, one of the Midwest's major carrier hotels, with access to more than 1,700 dark fiber strands and multiple Tier 1 carriers at sub two millisecond latency to that hub. Beyond the data center itself, the company has described plans for a 4,000 square foot smart greenhouse developed in partnership with Purdue University Northwest, suggesting an interest in agricultural technology tied to the campus's land or waste heat, though details of that project's status are not published. Digital Crossroad describes itself as a wholesale colocation company run by industry veterans, but does not publish a founding date or name specific customers on its site.

reading:
Digital Crossroad is the operating brand of a wholesale colocation facility at 100 Digital Crossroad Drive in Hammond, Indiana, built on the site of the former State Line Generating Plant, a coal fired power station on a peninsula at the Illinois and Indiana border. The site sits less than 30 minutes from downtown Chicago and, by the operator's account, under 12 fibre miles from the Chicago interconnection hub at 350 East Cermak, with access to more than 1,700 strands of dark fibre and sub two millisecond round trip latency.

The operator's published figures for the DX-1 building need to be kept apart from one another, because they describe different things. The building is 105,000 square feet with over 72,000 square feet of space available, and is stated to support up to 20 MW of IT capacity. Separately, the site has an on site substation rated at more than 100 MW, which is a utility capacity figure and not a measure of what the building can consume. Around 1 MW of on site solar generation is also claimed. Design PUE is given as 1.15 and rack density support as up to 25 kW per rack. Cooling uses Lake Michigan water side economisation, outside air, and refrigerant based Munters units. The design is described as Tier III concurrently maintainable, with ISO 27001 and SOC 2 compliance. A 10,000 square foot technology incubator occupies the former State Line archway building, which the company says once served as office space for Thomas Edison. Indiana House Bill 1405 provides a 50 year sales and use tax exemption, and the site carries an Opportunity Zone designation in Lake County.

The most important correction concerns CoreWeave. On 9 June 2025 the Hammond City Council voted eight to nil to approve a development agreement for a new data centre at 301 Digital Crossroads Drive, described by the city as the largest economic development project in Hammond's history. The city's own announcement stated that Decennial Group LLC built and still owns the existing 105,000 square foot data centre and would construct and own a new 450,000 square foot building on a 25 acre parcel branded the Data Center Peninsula, and quoted CoreWeave's co-founder describing a 180 megawatt facility. The city noted the project remained contingent on finalising a NIPSCO power agreement and executing a lease.

That agreement did not survive. On 1 July 2026 the City of Hammond announced that the development agreement had expired after two previously approved extensions, because milestones required by a 30 June 2026 deadline were not satisfied, and that no further extension would be offered. The four parties were the city, the Hammond Redevelopment Commission, Decennial Group and CoreWeave. The 180 MW figure therefore describes a lapsed proposal for a separate building, not capacity at this operator's facility, and should not be carried forward as either. It is also worth noting, on the city's own account, that Decennial Group rather than Digital Crossroad owns the existing building, so this operator record describes a brand and an operating business rather than a property owner.
